Done. Here is what happened and what the analysis shows.

## Important context on this run

The working directory was **not** empty at session start: it contained a complete prior pipeline (a 1479-line jupytext script, an executed notebook, 8 figures, CSVs, README) written at 11:23–11:35, plus a warm 6.7 GB stream cache. Rather than discard it or claim it uncritically, I audited the code, re-ran it end-to-end myself, and fixed a defect I found. Everything below is verified against runs I executed in this session.

## Verification performed

- **Code audit.** Real DANDI streaming only (no synthetic data anywhere), Allen default QC criteria, non-overlapping response windows asserted, permutation null that re-does the preferred-temporal-frequency selection inside every shuffle (so selection can't inflate the statistic), and a static-grating cross-check that is genuinely non-circular (units selected on drifting gratings, agreement measured on static).
- **Full re-run**, exit 0, reproduced every statistic bit-for-bit (e.g. Mann-Whitney U = 87387, p = 3.751e-43).
- **Read all 8 figures as images.** Found one real defect: in figure 2a the unconstrained double-von-Mises fit ran to ~100 Hz against a 15.6 Hz measured peak, because with 45° sampling a very large kappa needs a huge amplitude to match at the sampled points. It rescaled the polar axis and squashed the actual tuning curve to near-invisibility.
- **Fixed it** by capping kappa at the half-width the 45° sampling can resolve (kappa = ln2/(1−cos 22.5°) = 9.1), letting the measured points set the radial limit, and thinning the radial tick labels. Re-inspected: the two-lobed 90°/270° structure is now clearly legible.
- **Final notebook execution**: 38 cells, 0 errors, all figures regenerated from the final script.

## Result

Using **DANDI:000021** (Allen Institute Visual Coding, Neuropixels), six sessions with simultaneous LGd/VISp/higher-area coverage, 2516 QC-passing units:

Median global OSI rises from **0.091 in LGd to 0.252 in VISp** (p = 3.8e-43), and the significantly tuned fraction from **44.9% to 81.2%** (p = 6.9e-22). The ordering holds in all six mice individually. The preference is genuinely for orientation, not motion: preferred angle from 2 s drifting gratings and 250 ms static gratings differ by a median of 9.7° against a chance value of 45°. A cross-validated Poisson GLM shows direction still improves held-out prediction after running speed and temporal frequency are in the model. Thirty VISp units decode which of eight directions was shown at 63% (chance 12.5%), and the decoder's errors are **17× enriched at 180°**, which is the signature of an orientation code rather than a direction code.

One caveat the README states plainly: LGd is not perfectly untuned. A substantial minority reaches significance, so the thalamus-to-cortex difference is one of degree, though a large one.

Deliverables in the working directory: `orientation_selectivity_dandi.py`, `orientation_selectivity_dandi.ipynb`, `fig01`–`fig08` PNGs, `README.md`, plus `unit_metrics.csv` and `summary_by_area.csv`.
